sections.heading: C2 — Sharing roads with pedestrians, cyclists, motorcycles and large vehicles
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Sharing roads with pedestrians, cyclists, motorcycles and large vehicles

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A06
Before turning left across a motorcycle’s path, look again and establish the motorcycle’s position and speed. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A06
Do not assume a motorcycle’s flashing turn signal guarantees a turn; the rider may have left it on. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A06
When following a motorcycle below 40 mph, the handbook specifies a two-second gap. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A06
When following a motorcycle above 40 mph, the handbook specifies a four-second gap. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A06
Increase the motorcycle-following gap on a wet or slippery road. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A06
A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane; never drive alongside it within that lane even if there seems to be room. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A06
Allow extra room behind motorcycles in poor weather and watch for wet-surface glare that can hide the rider. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A06
Crosswinds and wind blasts from large trucks can cause sudden changes in a motorcycle’s speed or direction. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A06
Debris, gravel, pavement seams, animals or manhole covers can cause a motorcycle to change speed or course. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A06
A motorcycle rider may slow or alter course to meet angled railway tracks head-on and may rise from the seat over rough tracks. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A06
Metal or grated bridges can produce a motorcycle-tire wobble that prompts an inexperienced rider to slow or change direction. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A07
Animal riders and animal-drawn-vehicle drivers share motorists’ highway rights and duties except laws that cannot apply by their nature. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A07
Drivers of farm tractors and other self-propelled equipment have ordinary motorists’ highway rights and duties, with additional special requirements in a separate supplement. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A07
Vehicles that the DMV cannot register, such as minibikes, go-carts, golf carts, dirtbikes, motorized scooters and specified all-terrain vehicles, must not be driven on highways. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A07
The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is an orange fluorescent and reflective triangle; on seeing it, slow promptly and proceed carefully. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A07
Before passing a truck, check ahead and behind and enter the passing lane only where passing is legal and the lane is clear. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A07
If needed, blink the headlights to alert a truck driver before passing, particularly at night. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A08
Complete a pass promptly instead of remaining alongside the other vehicle. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A08
After passing a truck, a blink of its headlights can indicate clearance, but return only after seeing the truck’s front in the rear-view mirror. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A08
Maintain your speed after finishing a pass of a truck. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A08
When a truck passes, keep to the far side of your lane, consider slowing slightly and do not accelerate. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R22 | anchor: A08
When meeting an opposing truck, stay as far to your side as possible to reduce sideswipe risk and turbulence. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R23 | anchor: A08
The handbook says turbulence between meeting vehicles pushes them apart rather than drawing them together. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R24 | anchor: A08
A truck’s No-Zone refers to danger areas and blind spots around it where collisions are more likely. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R25 | anchor: A08
Keep a consistent speed while passing a large vehicle and wait until its cab appears in your rear-view mirror before moving ahead of it. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R26 | anchor: A08
Never pass closely behind a truck that is backing because both drivers can lose sight of one another in that area. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R27 | anchor: A08
A truck has a deep blind spot behind it; maintain at least four seconds of following space. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec11-R28 | anchor: A09
Trucks have large blind spots on both sides, so staying there can leave your vehicle unseen during a sudden lane change. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R29 | anchor: A09
A truck may swing left to turn right; do not cut between it and the curb or right shoulder. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R30 | anchor: A09
Do not cross behind a truck preparing to back into a loading area; wait rather than enter the driver’s blind spot. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0104]
